Flowers and pods per node of faba bean plants in a field trial

Source: R/data.R
FabaNodes26.Rd

This data set is not a growth curve and is not meant for the growth models of the package: it describes the pod set (pods per flower) of each node, e.g. for a binomial model as in the example. It belongs to the same field trial (2026) as FabaHeights26 and FabaFlowers26, with the same plants and Plant_ID, so that it can be merged with them, e.g. to relate the pod set of a plant to its height or to the timing of its flowering.

Usage

FabaNodes26

Format

A data frame with 879 rows and 11 variables:

Genotype

genotype: Navarra or Stella

Plot_ID

identifier of the plot

Plant_ID

identifier of the plant, as in FabaFlowers26 and FabaHeights26, e.g. "31_3"

Soil

soil type: Loamy or Sandy

Treatment

Irrigated or NotIrrigated

Node

node number on the stem

DAS_flowers

days after sowing of the count of the flowers of the node, NA without a flower record

Flowers

number of flowers of the node, NA if not counted

DAS_pods

days after sowing of the count of the pods of the node, NA without pods

Pods

number of pods of the node

Warning

1 if the record of the node cannot be right: more pods than flowers, or the pods counted on the same date as the flowers; 0 otherwise

Pods appear one to two weeks after flowering, so nodes that flowered in the last week of the counts may not have had the time to set pods. The raw data and the script that converts them, DIGIFABA_field_26.R, are in the directory data-raw of the source package.

Details

The flowers and pods of FabaFlowers26 by node instead of by date: one row for each node of the 96 plants that had flowers or pods, with the date and number of its flowers and the date and number of its pods, for the pod set (pods per flower) of each node. Each node was counted once, on the first date it had flowers and the first date it had pods; nodes counted again on a later date are left out of that date. A node that flowered but has no pod record set no pods (Pods = 0). The number of flowers is missing (NA) where the flowers of the node were not counted: a blank count, or pods on a node without a flower record.

Examples

# pod set per node by soil, irrigation and node position, from nodes with a reliable count
ok <- subset(FabaNodes26, !is.na(Flowers) & Warning == 0 & DAS_flowers <= 73)
fit <- glm(cbind(Pods, Flowers - Pods) ~ Soil * Treatment + Genotype + Node, family=binomial,
           data=ok)
summary(fit)
